clue.text: Minor member in pub taking it round in disguise

indicators.note: the small part sits inside the drinking establishment, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a cog in the machine is a minor member of an organisation
an inn is a pub
taken as written
a round letter, shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A junior club member goes round the pub in fancy dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor member' suggests a child in a club, but a cog is a small part of a bigger machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone travelling incognito hides their true identity, which is exactly being in disguise.

clue.text: Asian river does not end in dust

indicators.note: a word that does not end has lost its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: An Asian river never quite dries up to dust.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a major river flowing through Pakistan and India to the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: French dramatist caught in his water bed on top

indicators.note: the catch is placed inside the bed word, one within the other
in a down entry the bed sits above, so it comes first

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the Frenchman's water is eau

explanation.surface: A French playwright is found in his waterbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' refers back to the French dramatist, so the water is in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Cocteau was a French poet, playwright and film director of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Leave woman, top and toe, in this dress

indicators.note: head and foot of a down word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: to go is to leave
the opening and closing letters of woman

explanation.surface: A woman is told to walk out wearing this frock from head to foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A gown is a long formal garment worn by women, a type of dress.

clue.text: Garden flower in a kind of stew, nearly

indicators.note: nearly means not quite complete, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: Irish stew is a mutton and potato dish

explanation.surface: A garden flower almost ends up in a stew.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a popular perennial with sword-shaped leaves, grown widely in borders.

clue.text: Open University above criticism for swindling

indicators.note: in a down entry, being above means coming first in the order

blocks.note: OU is the abbreviation for the Open University
twitting is teasing reproach

explanation.surface: A university that is beyond reproach is accused of fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'above criticism' looks like a phrase meaning blameless; here it is positional.
explanation.definitionFit: Outwitting someone is getting the better of them by cunning, close to tricking or cheating them.

clue.text: Show contempt for cereal on Sunday

indicators.note: in an across entry, sitting on something means following it, so the grain word goes second

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for Sunday
corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at being served breakfast cereal on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'cereal on Sunday' means the cereal comes after the Sunday letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorn something is to treat it with disdain, the same verb as showing contempt for it.

clue.text: Oh! Decency's different with eg "New faces"

indicators.note: a different version of the letters is a new arrangement of them

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that decency has changed now that there are new faces about.
explanation.definitionFit: Synecdoche is the figure of speech using a part for the whole, as faces stands for people.

clue.text: Sea animal needing work after a month

indicators.note: the piece of work follows the month, fixing their order

blocks.note: OCT is the calendar abbreviation for October
opus is Latin for a work

explanation.surface: A marine creature needs a month of effort.
explanation.definitionFit: The octopus is an eight-armed marine mollusc, a creature living in the ocean.

clue.text: An unknown Spooner gets mixed up between two names

indicators.note: when things are mixed up their order is jumbled
the jumble sits with one letter on each side of it

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name, taken twice
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An obscure clergyman gets his words muddled between two names.
explanation.walkthrough: Spooner suggests a spoonerism, but here the name is simply anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonperson is someone of no importance or officially ignored, so effectively a nobody, an unknown.

clue.text: Lord Mayor says detective gets battering in Freetown

indicators.note: letters set free are released from their order and may fall into any arrangement
the beating is placed inside the rearranged settlement, so one goes within the other

blocks.note: dick is old slang for a private detective
the second half of this word is taken as written, to be rearranged; the first half is the signal to rearrange
a battering is a heavy hitting

explanation.surface: A city official reports that a detective was beaten up in the capital of Sierra Leone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freetown' looks like the African capital but splits in two: an instruction to rearrange, and the word to be rearranged around the beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Whittington, hero of the pantomime, was historically several times Lord Mayor of London.

clue.text: Footprint shows retreat of cat and dog

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the word is read in the backward direction

blocks.note: cats and dogs are typical household pets

explanation.surface: A paw print in the mud shows where the cat and dog backed away.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat and dog are examples of a category, not letters themselves; that category word turned round gives STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: A step can mean the mark left by a foot, as in footsteps in snow, so footprint matches.

clue.text: Tart married in church by pier without an end

indicators.note: lacking a final part means the last letter of the seaside structure is dropped

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for married
taken as written
CE stands for the Church of England
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: A loose woman marries in church beside a seaside pier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like an insult for a woman but is the pastry, a small Christmas pie.
explanation.definitionFit: A mince pie is a small sweet pastry filled with dried fruit, which is a kind of tart.

clue.text: Wild nut, highly flavoured

blocks.note: nut is slang for the head
a strong taste is a highly flavoured one

explanation.surface: A wild nut has a pungent taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nut' looks like food in this picture of flavours, but means the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Headstrong describes someone wilful and ungovernable, close to the sense of untamed behaviour.

clue.text: Make 100 and you've lost, corrupted with a jealous heart

indicators.note: something corrupted has been spoiled and altered, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricketer scores a century but still loses, and grows bitter with envy.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting covetously means wanting what others have, an envious frame of mind.

clue.text: I keep dressing with audacity, wanting love in the club

indicators.note: the round letter for nothing must go inside the sporting implement

blocks.note: sauce is cheeky impudence
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
a bat is a club used in sport

explanation.surface: Someone cheekily keeps getting dressed up at the club because they long for romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the object itself: a vessel that holds dressing, such as gravy or sauce, at table.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauceboat is a boat-shaped jug for serving gravy or sauce, which is a kind of dressing for food.

clue.text: Rascal finds Lily among the valuables

indicators.note: being among things means being placed in their midst

blocks.note: swag is stolen loot or valuables
the calla is a kind of lily

explanation.surface: A villain discovers a woman named Lily hiding among the treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lily' looks like a woman's name but is the flower; SCALLAWAG is a variant spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallawag or scallywag is a mischievous rogue, a playful word for a rascal.

clue.text: Make love to a half-sister in the spring

indicators.note: only half of the sibling word survives, the rest being cut away

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, like the letter O
taken as written
taken as written, then cut in half

explanation.surface: A scandalous suggestion of romance with a half-sibling in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-sister' reads as a relative but means the first half of the word sister.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile place in a desert fed by a spring or well of water.

clue.text: Change the people in the commercial

indicators.note: the folk are placed inside the advertisement, one word within the other

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial
men are people

explanation.surface: Swap the actors appearing in the TV advert.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text or law is to alter or correct it, a straightforward synonym for change.

clue.text: Pardon for former copper touching Sarah

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
Sal is a pet form of Sarah

explanation.surface: A retired policeman seeks forgiveness after laying hands on Sarah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' reads as a police officer, but means the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An excusal is a release from a duty or obligation, a kind of exemption or pardon.

clue.text: Dine poorly by hot cooker in the Netherlands

definitions.note: the definition describes where the city is rather than naming a place noun

indicators.note: doing something poorly means it comes out badly arranged, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
an oven is a cooker

explanation.surface: Someone eats badly beside a hot stove while on holiday in Holland.
explanation.definitionFit: Eindhoven is a large Dutch city, home of Philips and PSV football club, located in that country.

clue.text: High quality "6 no-trumps" made with maturity

blocks.note: VI is the Roman numeral for six
NT is the bridge abbreviation for no trumps
age is maturity

explanation.surface: A top bridge bid of six no-trumps is made by an experienced player.
explanation.definitionFit: Vintage describes something of lasting excellence, as in a fine wine from a good year.

clue.text: Place an adder in medicinal liquid

indicators.note: the accountant goes inside the medicinal fluid, one word within the other

blocks.note: a lotion is a liquid applied to the skin as medicine
a chartered accountant, CA, is someone who adds up figures

explanation.surface: Someone drops a snake into a bottle of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adder' looks like the snake but means one who adds, an accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: A location is a particular spot or site, the noun sense of the word place.

clue.text: United Nations party is free

blocks.note: UN is the abbreviation for United Nations
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A celebration hosted by the United Nations costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' reads as an adjective meaning no charge, but here it is the verb to release.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot or fastening is to loosen and release it, the verb sense of free.

clue.text: Plump duck to be seen half done

indicators.note: only half the word is completed, so the second half is cut away

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, like the letter O
taken as written; that the letters also run through 'to be seen' is a coincidence of the setter's charade
taken as written, then halved

explanation.surface: A fat duck looks only half cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a batsman's score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very overweight, a stronger synonym for plump or fat.

clue.text: Tree not lying in bed, though

blocks.note: someone up has risen from bed

explanation.definitionFit: The upas is a poisonous Javan tree whose sap was used for arrow poison.

clue.text: Easy-going and available for nothing

blocks.note: first meaning: relaxed and unrestricted
second meaning: costing no money

explanation.surface: Something relaxed and also without charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both unconstrained in manner and costing nothing, two common adjective senses.

clue.text: Dame Rebecca riding very good horse in Somerset

definitions.note: the definition gives the town's location rather than a place noun

riding a horse means being on it

a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A famous novelist rides an excellent horse through the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Weston-super-Mare is a seaside resort town on the Bristol Channel coast of that English county.

clue.text: Silence enshrouds upper and lower prison camps

clue.text: Severe yet devious last night

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged
